claims.text: The proposed material is a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
The initial material has a homogeneous, single-phase microstructure without pre-formed nanoprecipitates.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitates can be introduced into tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
Controlled thermal treatments or alloying can be used to produce the proposed coherent nanoprecipitates.
The relevant structural mediator is a dispersion of nanoprecipitates having coherent interfaces with the matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations that can cause premature crack initiation.
The reduction in stress concentration specifically results from reduced lattice-mismatch stresses.
Coherent nanoprecipitates delay crack propagation.
Formation of coherent nanoprecipitates governs high-temperature plastic strain in tungsten-based refractory alloys.
Formation of coherent nanoprecipitates governs high-temperature toughness in tungsten-based refractory alloys.
Relative to a precipitate-free baseline, the SCCP alloy will have greater tensile plastic strain at elevated temperature.
Relative to a precipitate-free baseline, the SCCP alloy will have greater toughness and energy absorption before failure at elevated temperature.
The cited SCCP alloy exhibits 15% tensile ductility at ambient temperature and a yield strength of 1.05 GPa at 800 °C.
The proposed mechanism applies under tensile or creep loading from ambient temperature to approximately 800 °C.
The mechanism is expected to apply to tungsten-based refractory alloys under fusion-relevant operating conditions up to about 800 °C.
Applicability outside the tungsten-based alloy system or stated temperature range is uncertain.
The magnitude of improvement and its sensitivity to precipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction require experimental validation.
Toughness can be evaluated as the area under the stress-strain curve.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in both plastic strain and toughness relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
